blocks.text: The true cost of poor boundary management

When you lack boundaries, you pay in time and mental health. Property managers often act as the central node for all information. This creates an unhealthy dependency where your portfolio relies on your memory. You spend your day chasing information across emails, texts, and phone calls. This reactive cycle keeps you in a state of constant stress. It makes it impossible to focus on strategic tasks like owner reporting or lease renewals.

The role is relentlessly reactive. You absorb frustration from both tenants and landlords. This is a textbook recipe for chronic stress. Information is often trapped in fragmented records. You end up spending hours each day manually transcribing maintenance requests into spreadsheets. Without clear, enforced policies, you feel pressured to be available 24/7. This prevents you from ever truly switching off.
Fixes for boundary management without buying new tools

items: Use macOS Focus modes to silence notifications during non-working hours.
Set up an auto-reply in Gmail or Outlook that directs tenants to your portal for maintenance requests.
Stop using your personal phone number for work; use a dedicated business line or app.
Schedule specific times for email triage rather than checking it 15 times per day.
Create standard templates for common tenant responses in your email client.

faq.question: How can I stop checking email so often?
faq.answer: Schedule two or three specific times in your day to process your inbox. Use macOS Focus modes to block notifications from your email app outside of those times.

faq.question: Is it possible to set boundaries with tenants?
faq.answer: Yes, by directing all maintenance and non-urgent inquiries to a centralized portal. This removes the need for ad-hoc communication via text or personal email.
